role: rival comparison on questions Graph-MIND was never tuned against

pool.why_clean: read only by its own untouched eval; 18 scripts read v3.2 instead

order: sha256(question_id) ascending; a prefix may be reported if the run is cut short

mem0.parameters: its own defaults: temperature 0.1, top_p 0.1, max_tokens 2000
deviations: model named explicitly as gpt-4o-mini. Mem0 2.2.1's defaults cannot all hold at once: its default model is gpt-5-mini, which its reasoning-model list omits, so it sends temperature=0.1 and OpenAI returns 400. Its parameter block is written for a model that accepts those parameters, so the parameters were kept and a model that takes them was named
mem0ai[extras], mem0ai[nlp], en_core_web_sm installed so BM25 hybrid search and spaCy are ON, as its docs intend
mem0.write_tokens: measured, not inferred: every OpenAI call it makes is intercepted and its usage summed (write-usage.jsonl)
mem0.input: the FULL haystack, ~48 sessions per question, which is MORE than Graph-MIND extracts in this harness (only the retrieved sessions)

graph_mind_product.what: the recall path the MCP server ships (brain_context), not the benchmark pipeline: no write-time LLM; the haystack stored as captured turns
graph_mind_product.retrieval: USER turns cut into 500-char pieces ranked by local embeddings, fused by reciprocal rank with SQLite full-text search; hits delivered as their 500-char piece; assistant answers delivered whole (<=3000 chars) when the question is about what the assistant said
graph_mind_product.about_assistant: set by the calling model in real use; played here by the benchmark's own stand-in (asks_assistant_history regex)
graph_mind_product.dev2_reference: 88.3% on the tuned dev2 set vs benchmark pipeline 85.8%, McNemar p=0.68

hypothesis: Graph-MIND's evidence reaches the reader more often than Mem0's or MemPalace's, on questions none of the three was tuned on.
reported_regardless: the accuracy of all three, per question type, with the per-question judge verdicts, whatever the ordering turns out to be
noise_floor: 9 of 120 answers move between identical runs (REPORT.md section 6), so at n=40 a gap under about 8 points is not interpretable

supersedes.reason_for_amendment: product_recall_eval.fill() now skips empty turns, as the capture service it imitates always has (conversation_memory skips a turn whose text is blank). LongMemEval has a few empty turns; the store rejected them (CONTENT_REDACTED_REQUIRED) and the product arm's packet build stopped at question 33 of 40. No answer or judgement exists for any arm; the 32 packets already built are unaffected because the skipped turns hold no text.
